text: Process Architecture L0 — Procurement L0-Procurement · level 0 · the enterprise process framework The enterprise procurement process framework. Twenty-five processes across six domains, expressed as text-first process objects that are versioned in Git, published through the management system, and served to AI agents over MCP with explicit delegation boundaries. --- Purpose This framework is the connective tissue of procurement: it links what the enterprise intends (strategy, policies) to what happens (processes), to how it is judged (skills), to what is produced (templates), and it makes every one of those things legible to an AI agent with a defined and auditable mandate. title: Intake Management
summary: Captures every demand for goods and services at the point of origin, qualifies it against strategy and budget, and routes it to the right buying channel — so that only valid, funded, approved requests reach sourcing.
path: Procurement > Intake Management
text: Intake Management IM · L1-IntakeManagement · level 1 domain Captures every demand for goods and services at the point of origin, qualifies it against strategy and budget, and routes it to the right buying channel — so that only valid, funded, approved requests reach sourcing. --- Purpose Intake Management is the front door of procurement. It exists to stop three specific failures: buying what the business already has, buying without a funding decision, and buying outside the approved channel. It is also where the majority of avoidable sourcing cycles are eliminated. Scope In scope - Guided intake of purchase requirements from any function - Catalogue and contract-first recommendation - Demand consolidation and de-duplication - Qualification against category strategy, budget and approval thresholds - Routing to sourcing, catalogue purchase, or rejection Out of scope - Category strategy definition (Proc 1.2) - Sourcing event execution (Proc 3.1) - Requisition approval (Proc 4.1) Entry criteria - Category strategy published for the requested category - Budget lines loaded for the requesting function Exit criteria - Request qualified and routed to a buying channel - Rejection reasons recorded where applicable Processes in this domain ID Process Purpose AI ceiling --- --- --- --- Proc 2.1 Request to Buying Channel Captures a purchase requirement, qualifies it against strategy, budget and thresholds, matches it to existing catalogue and contract supply, and routes it to the correct buying channel — or rejects it with a reason L3 Proc 2.2 Demand Management Consolidates, de-duplicates, analyses and shapes demand across the enterprise so that sourcing runs against a clear, aggregated picture rather than a stream of isolated requests L3 Flow Systems System Role in this domain Category --- --- --- Coupa Intake Guided intake and requisition capture coupa Coupa Procurement Requisition to purchase order coupa SAP S/4HANA Financial and operational ledger erp Microsoft Teams Collaboration and approvals collaboration Domain delegation profile Domain KPIs KPI Definition Target --- --- --- Intake to requisition conversion Share of intake requests that become a requisition rather than being rejected or abandoned 70% Catalogue hit rate Share of intake requests resolved from an approved catalogue 45% Requisition touch time Elapsed time from intake submission to approved requisition < 2 business days Risks Risk Control --- --- Requests are split across intakes to stay below approval thresholds Detect and consolidate split requests at the requester level and refer them for review Buyers are bypassed through informal channels Catalogue-first routing and block payment for spend without a compliant requisition Related - title: Invoice to Pay
summary: Receives supplier invoices, matches them against the purchase order and receipt, resolves exceptions, and releases payment — with a proportionate, always-on control against duplicate and fraudulent payment.
path: Procurement > Invoice to Pay
text: Invoice to Pay I2P · L1-InvoiceToPay · level 1 domain Receives supplier invoices, matches them against the purchase order and receipt, resolves exceptions, and releases payment — with a proportionate, always-on control against duplicate and fraudulent payment. --- Purpose Invoice to Pay is where the organisation either captures or loses the value negotiated upstream. The design goal is that the happy path is entirely automated and exception-free, and that every exception is handled by a human with the context to resolve it quickly. Scope In scope - Invoice capture from all channels including e-invoicing - Duplicate, fraud and sanctions screening - Three-way match and tolerance handling - Exception resolution and recovery - Payment scheduling and release Out of scope - Purchase order creation (Proc 4.2) - Goods receipt confirmation (Proc 4.3) - Supplier commercial terms renegotiation (Proc 1.6) Entry criteria - PO issued (or a documented non-PO basis) - Supplier banking data validated and current Exit criteria - Payment released and remittance sent - Invoice and payment evidence archived Processes in this domain ID Process Purpose AI ceiling --- --- --- --- Proc 5.1 Receive Invoice Captures supplier invoices from every channel, validates their structure, screens them for duplication, fraud and sanctions exposure, and routes them into the matching process L2 Proc 5.2 Match and Approve Invoice Matches the invoice against the purchase order and the goods receipt, evaluates variances against defined tolerances, routes the invoice for approval, and releases it into the payment run L3 Proc 5.3 Resolve Invoice Issue Classifies invoice exceptions, assigns them to the right owner with the context to act, resolves them — by correcting, disputing, writing off or cancelling — and feeds the recurring root cause back into process improvement L2 Proc 5.4 Pay Invoice Schedules approved invoices into payment runs, applies early-payment discounts and run optimisations, verifies supplier banking data independently, releases payment and sends remittance advice L2 Flow Systems System Role in this domain Category --- --- --- Coupa Invoicing Invoice capture, matching, exceptions coupa SAP S/4HANA Financial and operational ledger erp SAP Tax Management Determination and tax compliance finance Microsoft Teams Collaboration and approvals collaboration Domain delegation profile Domain KPIs KPI Definition Target --- --- --- Straight-through processing rate Share of invoices paid without any human touch 80% Cost per invoice Total accounts payable operating cost divided by invoices processed tracked, trending down Exception resolution time Elapsed working days from invoice submission to exception cleared < 5 days Risks Risk Control --- --- Payment redirection fraud via changed bank details Dual-channel verification of bank changes, independent of the change requester Duplicate invoices paid twice Probabilistic duplicate detection plus a duplicate invoice hold list Related - title: AI Delegation Matrix
summary: The canonical definition of how much freedom an AI agent is granted to perform a task and make decisions. Every process, skill and template in this framework declares a delegation level. This document is the authority those declarations resolve against.
text: AI Delegation Matrix Why this exists. "AI may assist in procurement" is not a mandate. A mandate is actionable , bounded , enforceable and auditable . This document supplies the vocabulary for all four. If a step in this framework does not declare a delegation level, the process is not deployable — the validator rejects it. --- 1. The five delegation levels Levels describe who decides , not how much the AI is used. Level Name The AI may The human must Typical spend exposure ------- ------ ------------- --------------- ----------------------- L0 Observe Read, classify, extract, summarise, compare, flag Decide and act Any L1 Draft Produce a draft artefact for a human to edit and approve Review, edit, approve, execute Any L2 Execute with approval Perform system actions in a sandbox, then wait at a named checkpoint Approve at the checkpoint Bounded L3 Execute within mandate Perform system actions autonomously inside hard thresholds Monitor, and review the audit log Bounded and pre-authorised L4 Decide Make a bounded judgement call from a defined candidate set Audit, and periodically review the decision space Bounded, discretionary band The ceiling rule. The effective level of any step is the minimum of: A process can only ever narrow the delegation granted by the organisation-wide policy; it can never widen it. framework/policies/policy ai delegation of record.md sets the organisational ceilings. --- 2. Authority verbs Every delegation declaration pairs a level with an authority verb . The verb is what appears in the audit log and what the MCP server reports to a calling agent. Verb Meaning Reversible? ------ --------- ------------- observe Read-only. No state change anywhere. n/a draft Produces an artefact (text, table, proposal). No transaction. Yes — discard recommend Produces a ranked recommendation with rationale. No transaction. Yes — discard prepare Stages a transaction (e.g. creates a PO in draft) without submitting. Yes — cancel execute Submits a transaction that changes state. Only if the domain supports reversal decide Selects among candidate options and commits to one. Only if reversible by policy Irreversibility is the real risk boundary. An execute step that charges a supplier's bank account is not equivalent to one that writes a draft to a staging area. The reversible flag is therefore mandatory and is checked by the validator. --- 3. The decision space The decision space is the bounded set of choices an agent is permitted to make. It is expressed as four orthogonal controls: Four rules govern the decision space: 1. Closed sets. must select from is closed. If the agent cannot find an acceptable candidate inside the set, it must escalate — it must never widen the set itself. 2. Numeric thresholds decide autonomy. If a threshold applies to the step, the agent is L3 below the threshold and L2 above it. Threshold crossing is evaluated before the action, never after. 3. Prohibited is absolute. prohibited is not a default suggestion. It is enforced by the policy gateway before the action is dispatched. 4. Escalation band is a subset of prohibited ambiguity. If the agent is unsure whether a value falls inside or outside the band, it escalates. --- 4. Constraints, guardrails, escalation Three different things, three different enforcement points: Element Question it answers Enforced by When --------- -------------------- -------------- ------ constraints What must be true for this step to run at all? Pre-flight validator Before the step starts guardrails Which policies and controls constrain the action? Policy gateway Before every action escalation When does the agent hand control back to a human? Orchestrator Continuously Escalation is a first-class outcome. An agent that escalates has succeeded at its job. Systems that punish escalation produce agents that guess — the single largest source of governance risk in agentic procurement. --- 5. Evidence and audit Delegation without evidence is delegation without accountability. Every step that declares execute or decide must declare the evidence it produces: The audit record is what lets the process-auditing companion propose improvements later, and what lets an external AI agent's decisions be re-examined months afterwards. --- 6. Data classification ceiling An agent may never process data above the classification ceiling of the step it is acting in, regardless of its capability or the level granted. Classification Typical content Autonomous agent permitted? ---------------- ----------------- ----------------------------- public Published tender notices, supplier websites Yes, up to L3 internal Process definitions, playbooks, internal KPIs Yes, up to L3 confidential Supplier pricing, contract terms, negotiation positions L2 maximum unless explicitly mandated restricted Personal data, national-security-adjacent data, M&A targets L1 maximum — always a human restricted is a hard stop. No delegation level, no mandate and no exception may authorise an autonomous agent to act on restricted data. This is the one rule in this matrix that cannot be overridden locally. --- 7. Setting the levels: who decides what Level change Who How -------------- ----- ----- Draft a process with a level Process owner + co-design community PR against the framework repo Raise a level within an existing mandate Delegation Review Board Delegation RFC, quarterly window Set an organisational ceiling Procurement Governance + Risk Change to policy ai delegation of record Emergency suspension of a level Any governance role Incident record + post-incident review Levels expire. A delegation granted at L3 without a review cadence and a reviewer is downgraded to L2 automatically by the validator. Delegation is a lease, not a permanent right — that is what keeps it honest. --- 8. Worked examples An agent triaging an invoice that does not match the PO → L0, Observe. summary: The mandatory human checkpoints in the procurement value chain, and the AI delegation ceiling permitted at each one. A control point is where an agent is structurally required to stop and hand control back to a named human role.
text: Control Points A control point is a named place in the process where the AI agent must stop. Control points are the mechanism that turns "AI-assisted procurement" into "governed procurement". title: Glossary
summary: The shared vocabulary of the framework. Every term below is used with exactly this meaning in a process, a policy, a skill and a template, so that a practitioner and an agent are talking about the same thing.
text: Glossary The framework is only useful if the same word means the same thing in every document. This is that list. --- The framework itself Process object — the unit of the framework: a markdown file with structured front matter (identity, ownership, taxonomy, inputs, outputs, relations, AI delegation, audit) and a structured body (purpose, scope, steps, decision criteria, policies, skills, templates, KPIs, risks, exceptions, change log). The front matter is what a machine reads; the body is what a human reads. Both live in one file so they cannot drift apart. L0 / L1 / L2 — the three levels of the hierarchy. L0 is the enterprise architecture: the whole map, the cross-domain flows, the enterprise KPIs. L1 is a domain: a coherent area of procurement with its own entry and exit criteria, such as Source-to-Contract or Invoice-to-Pay. L2 is a process: a unit of work with a trigger, a defined output and a named owner. A step inside a process is not a level — it is a directive. Hierarchy edge — a containment relation. "Proc 4.1 is contained in Purchase to Order, which is contained in the enterprise architecture." Flow edge — a value flow. "A completed purchase order flows to Goods Receipt." Flow edges point upstream to downstream, and they are what breaks when information has to be chased by hand. Governs edge — a constraint. "Policy X governs Proc 4.1", "Skill Y governs Proc 3.2", "Template Z governs the artefact produced by Proc 5.3." Process Architecture L0 — the map of the whole framework, rendered as text and as a graph. It is the answer to "where am I?" --- AI delegation AI Delegation Model (ADM) — the framework's model of how much freedom an agent has. Five levels, a decision space, three enforcement points and a rule that escalation is a success. Level (L0–L4) — how much freedom the agent has at a given step. Level Name The agent may ------- ------ --------------- L0 Observe Read, classify, summarise, flag. L1 Draft Produce artefacts a human edits and approves. L2 Execute with approval Act, but stop at a named human checkpoint. L3 Execute within mandate Act autonomously inside hard thresholds. L4 Decide Make a bounded judgement call from a closed candidate set. Ceiling rule — effective = min(process ceiling, step level) , hard-capped at L1 for restricted data. A step can ask for more than its process allows; it will not get it. Authority verb — what the agent is permitted to do , as distinct from how much freedom it has. The verbs are observe , draft , recommend , prepare , execute , decide . Decision space — the boundary of what the agent may decide: the candidate set it may choose from, the numeric thresholds that decide its autonomy, the actions that are prohibited outright, and the band in which it must escalate. Constraint — a precondition checked before a step runs. "The requisition is qualified." A constraint is about the world; a guardrail is about the act. Guardrail — a policy check applied at the point of action, by the policy gateway. "Do not issue a purchase order without a recorded approval." Escalation — the hand-over route when a trigger fires. It names the target role and the service level. Escalation is a successful outcome : an agent that escalates has done its job, and the audit trail records the hand-over rather than a failure. Human checkpoint — the point at which a human must take over. always , required , on exception or never . Evidence — the record that an action happened: what was done, under which version of which policy, with which supporting artefacts. An action without evidence did not happen. Data classification — how sensitive the data is: public , internal , confidential or restricted . The classification caps the level: restricted is a hard stop at L1. Delegation Register — the list of places in the framework where an agent holds more than L2. A delegation above L2 is a lease , not a grant: it names a reviewer, a review cadence, and the steps it covers, and it comes back to the Delegation Review Board when the lease expires. Control point (CP-x) — a named place in the value chain where an agent is structurally required to stop. Fourteen of them, listed in [ Control-Points.md ](./Control-Points.md). Delegation Review Board — the body that grants, reviews and withdraws delegations. Its composition and cadence are set out in the Control Points document. --- Procurement Intake — the request entering the organisation. The place where demand is qualified against strategy, budget and thresholds before anything else happens. Channel strategy — the rule that decides whether a request is served from the catalogue, from a contract, through a tender, or directly. Catalogue — the pre-approved list of items or services that can be ordered without a new sourcing event. Bid — a supplier's response to a request for quotation or proposal. Three-way match — the control that compares the invoice to the purchase order and to the goods receipt before payment. The match itself is arithmetic; the approval and the payment release are human. Goods receipt note (GRN) — the record that goods or services were received. It is the third leg of the three-way match. Service entry sheet (SES) — the record that a service was received and accepted, where no physical goods exist. Debit note — a document that reduces an invoice rather than requesting payment. Supplier risk — the assessed likelihood and impact of a supplier failing to deliver. Classified on a published scale, which is what makes it delegable. Conditional approval — a supplier is approved to trade, with stated conditions (volume caps, enhanced monitoring, a defined review date) rather than being approved outright. Offboarding — the controlled removal of a supplier from the active population: no new orders, final invoices settled, personal and system access revoked, master data archived. Material master — the record that defines an item: its description, its plant of record, its classification, the rules that govern it. Master

title: Agent Access to the Process Framework
text: Agent Access to the Process Framework policy agent access and mcp · ai-governance policy · version 1.0.0 Governs how external and internal AI agents discover, read and act upon the process framework over MCP, including scoping, versioning, rate limits and audit. --- Purpose Serving the framework over MCP is what turns it from documentation into infrastructure. That is exactly why access needs rules: an agent that can read the framework can also discover the delegation ceilings, the escalation routes and the templates — and therefore needs to be a known, scoped actor. Statement All access to the process framework by an AI agent shall be authenticated, scoped to named processes and named tools, and logged. Agents shall be served only process objects with an active status. The framework version in force at the moment of execution shall be recorded with the resulting decision, so that any historical action can be replayed against the rules that applied at the time. Rules - Every agent holds a scoped credential identifying the agent, its owner and its permitted tools. - The MCP server serves only published, validated process objects with status active . - Every tool response embeds the framework version and the delegation ceiling that applies. - Agent queries are logged with the identity of the calling agent and the returned context. - A supplier-side agent may be granted access to the supplier-facing subset only. - Rate limits and context budgets apply per agent. Applies to None. Enforcement Rationale The version-in-force requirement is what makes the framework auditable. Without it, an action taken under last year's delegation cannot be judged against last year's rules — and the audit becomes opinion. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - mcp access log - framework version stamps - agent registry Related None. title: AI Delegation of Record
text: AI Delegation of Record policy ai delegation of record · ai-governance policy · version 1.0.0 Sets the organisational ceilings for AI delegation, the conditions under which each level may be granted, and the review and revocation mechanism that keeps delegation a lease rather than a permanent right. --- Purpose Delegation without limits is abdication. This policy defines what "AI may assist" means in enforceable terms, so that a process owner granting an L3 delegation is doing so within a known envelope, and an auditor can reconstruct what was permitted at any point in time. Statement No AI agent shall act with a delegation level exceeding the ceiling declared for the process, nor exceeding the ceiling for the data classification it is acting upon. Restricted-classification data shall never be processed autonomously, irrespective of any delegation granted. A delegation shall be granted only where the process declares an explicit decision space, escalation trigger and evidence requirement, and shall lapse if unreviewed at the end of its review cadence. Rules - L0 and L1 may be granted by any process owner within the framework. - L2 requires a published decision space and an escalation trigger, and approval by the Delegation Review Board chair. - L3 requires approval by the full Delegation Review Board, a hard numeric threshold, and a named human reviewer. - L4 requires full Board approval, a closed candidate set, mandatory decision rationale, and monthly audit sampling. - Any delegation may be suspended immediately by the chair, the CISO or the Finance Controller. - A delegation without a reviewer and a review cadence is downgraded automatically to L2. Applies to - - Proc 1.1 - - Proc 1.4 - - Proc 3.1 - - Proc 3.2 - - Proc 4.1 - - Proc 4.2 - - Proc 5.1 - - Proc 5.2 - - Proc 5.4 - - Proc 6.1 - - Proc 6.3 Enforcement Rationale Autonomous agents are most valuable exactly where they are least supervised — high volume, low value, rule-bound decisions. Capping delegation at those points, and making every grant reviewable, converts AI from an unbounded risk into a managed capability. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - delegation register - review board minutes - suspension log Related None. title: Catalogue and Contract First
text: Catalogue and Contract First policy catalog first · sourcing policy · version 1.0.0 Requires that existing catalogue items and contracted supply are exhausted before new sourcing is initiated, and that any departure from them is measured and justified. --- Purpose Contract leakage — buying what is already under contract at a higher price — is the single largest source of value erosion in a mature procurement function. Catalogue-first makes the default path the cheapest path. Statement Every purchase requirement shall be matched against approved catalogue items and active contracts before being routed to a sourcing event. Where a requirement cannot be met from existing supply, the departure shall be recorded with its value consequence and reviewed as part of contract coverage reporting. Rules - Matching is performed at intake and re-performed before purchase order issue. - A catalogue order above the delegated value threshold requires human confirmation of the match. - Payment shall be blocked for spend without a compliant requisition, except where a documented non-PO basis exists. - Contract coverage rate is reported monthly by category. Applies to - - Proc 2.1 - - Proc 4.1 - - Proc 4.2 Enforcement Rationale Coverage is only a target if it is enforced at the moment of ordering. Blocking at intake and at PO issue makes the rule structural rather than advisory. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - catalogue match log - contract coverage report Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Competitive Tendering
text: Competitive Tendering policy competitive tendering · sourcing policy · version 1.0.0 Requires competition for material spend, sets the pre-commissioning discipline that makes an award defensible, and defines the circumstances in which a single source is permitted. --- Purpose Competition is the mechanism that converts supplier willingness to pay into captured value. But competition without discipline is theatre: criteria drifting after bids arrive, or a shortlist that was never really open. This policy governs both the requirement to compete and the pre-commissioning discipline. Statement Spend above the competitive threshold shall be awarded through a competitive process with a minimum of three invited suppliers, unless a single source is justified and approved at award level. Evaluation criteria, weighting and the supplier shortlist shall be approved and locked before the event is published. Any change to locked criteria after publication voids the event. Rules - The competitive threshold is defined by category and reviewed annually. - Requirements, evaluation criteria, weighting and shortlist are approved before publication. - Locked criteria are stored with a cryptographic hash; divergence is detectable. - A single-source award requires a written justification from one of: sole-source capability, intellectual property, regulatory constraint, or documented market failure. - Clarifications are issued to all participants, never to one. - A single-bid outcome requires justification at award level and is reported. Applies to - - Proc 3.1 - - Proc 3.2 Enforcement Rationale The lock is the point. An award defended on criteria that were decided after the bids are visible is not defensible, and it teaches suppliers that the process is negotiable. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - rfx publication log - criteria lock hash - single source justifications Related None. title: Contract Management
text: Contract Management policy contract management · compliance policy · version 1.0.0 Requires that contracts be executed from approved templates, that deviations from the template be reviewed, and that obligations inside executed contracts be tracked rather than assumed. --- Purpose A contract without an obligation register is a document, not a control. This policy makes the executed contract a live object with tracked obligations, and it prevents bespoke paper from quietly replacing the standards that protect the organisation. Statement Contracts shall be executed from approved templates. Any deviation from a template clause shall be recorded in the deviation register and reviewed by Legal. On execution, the contract's obligations — dates, notice periods, escalators, service levels and renewal terms — shall be extracted into a tracked obligation register. Rules - Only approved templates may be used for contracts above the low-value threshold. - Deviations from standard clauses require Legal review and are recorded with the rationale. - Obligation extraction is mandatory and must complete within 24 hours of execution. - Renewal and notice dates generate automated reminders at 180, 120 and 60 days. - Commercial terms may not be varied away from the award without a recorded approval. Applies to - - Proc 3.3 - - Proc 3.5 - - Proc 4.1 - - Proc 4.2 - - Proc 1.6 - - Proc 6.4 Enforcement Rationale Terms negotiated but unenforced, and obligations known but untracked, are the two ways a well-negotiated contract still fails. Automation of obligation capture is the highest-leverage intervention available. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - deviation register - obligation register - renewal reminder log Related None. title: Data Classification and AI Handling
text: Data Classification and AI Handling policy data classification · security policy · version 1.0.0 Classifies procurement data, caps what an AI agent may process at each level, and requires that agent access to the framework itself be governed and logged. --- Purpose Delegation is meaningless without a data ceiling. A process that grants an L3 delegation is only safe if the data it acts upon is appropriately classified — and some data may never be processed autonomously at all. Statement Procurement data shall be classified as public, internal, confidential or restricted. An AI agent shall not process data classified above the ceiling declared for the step it is acting in. Data classified as restricted shall never be processed by an agent acting autonomously, irrespective of any delegation granted. Agent access to the process framework shall be authenticated, scoped and logged. Rules - Every process input, output and step declares a data classification. - Restricted data caps any agent at L1, always. - Confidential data caps autonomous agents at L2 unless a specific delegation from the Delegation Review Board states otherwise. - Agent access tokens are scoped per agent, per process and per time period. - All agent queries to the framework are logged and available for audit. Applies to - - Proc 1.1 - - Proc 1.2 - - Proc 3.1 - - Proc 3.2 - - Proc 3.3 - - Proc 5.1 - - Proc 5.4 - - Proc 6.1 - - Proc 6.3 Enforcement Rationale Most agent incidents are context assembly failures rather than model failures: an agent given more data than the step warrants. The classification ceiling makes the context assembly itself a controlled act. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - classification declarations - access log - context assembly log Related None. title: Fraud and Duplicate Control
text: Fraud and Duplicate Control policy fraud and duplicate control · compliance policy · version 1.0.0 Sets the controls that protect against payment redirection, duplicate payment and false invoicing, including the independent verification requirement for supplier banking data. --- Purpose Payment fraud is cheap to commit and expensive to detect after settlement. The controls that stop it are unglamorous: independent verification, duplicate detection, combination screening and a release that requires two people. Statement Changes to supplier banking data shall be verified through a channel independent of the request. Payment release shall require dual control. Invoices shall be screened for duplication, and a screening hold shall only be cleared by a named human. Combination signals — a recent bank change together with an unusual invoice — shall be treated as a hold trigger regardless of individual severity. Rules - Bank-detail changes are verified by callback to a previously held contact number, never to a number on the change request. - Payment release requires dual authorisation; an agent may never release a payment. - Duplicate screening uses probabilistic matching; a hold is cleared only by a human with a recorded reason. - Payment recalls are blocked at the supplier level pending fraud investigation. - Hold volumes, release reasons and overrides are audited monthly. Applies to - - Proc 5.1 - - Proc 5.2 - - Proc 5.3 - - Proc 5.4 - - Proc 6.1 Enforcement Rationale The verification channel is the whole control. Every real payment-redirection fraud exploited a channel that was not independent of the request — a reply-all email, a number in the request, a known contact who was also the requester. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - bank verification record - dual control record - hold release log Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Intake Quality
text: Intake Quality policy intake quality · operational policy · version 1.0.0 Sets the completeness standard for purchase requests and the requirement that a request be specific enough to be sourced without further clarification. --- Purpose Vague requests are the largest single driver of procurement cycle time. They cause back-and-forth, incomplete RFx packages, mis-scoped contracts and disputes. Quality at intake pays for itself many times over downstream. Statement A purchase request shall state the business need, the specification, the quantity or volume, the required date, the cost centre and the budget holder. A request that does not meet the completeness standard shall be returned to the requester with the specific missing fields identified, and shall not be progressed by procurement staff on the requester's behalf. Rules - The completeness standard is defined per category and published. - A request must be able to be sourced without asking the requester a further question about specification, volume or date. - Return-for-correction is a designed outcome, not a failure, and is measured as such. - The share of requests requiring clarification at the sourcing stage is a supplier-quality indicator of intake quality. Applies to - - Proc 2.1 - - Proc 2.2 - - Proc 4.1 Enforcement Rationale Procurement staff filling in a requester's specification is hidden work that hides risk: the resulting contract no longer reflects what the business actually needs, and nobody owns the gap. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - intake completeness report - return for correction log Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Master Data Quality
text: Master Data Quality policy master data quality · operational policy · version 1.0.0 Sets the quality standard for supplier, material and catalogue master data, and requires that incomplete or duplicated records be remediated rather than tolerated. --- Purpose Automation is only as good as the data it operates on. An agent reasoning over a supplier record with a stale tax identifier is not wrong in an obvious way — it is confidently wrong, which is worse. Master data quality is therefore a control, not housekeeping. Statement All master data records shall be complete, unique, current and attributable. A record failing a mandatory data-quality rule shall not be used in an automated transaction until remediated. Records shall carry provenance for every field that originates outside the organisation. Rules - Mandatory completeness, uniqueness, validity and currency rules are published per object type. - A record failing a blocking rule may not be used in an automated transaction. - Externally sourced fields record their provenance and retrieval date. - Data quality is measured continuously and reported by owner. - Remediation is prioritised by the business impact of the records affected, not by record count. Applies to - - Proc 3.4 - - Proc 3.5 - - Proc 6.1 - - Proc 6.3 Enforcement Rationale Blocking on quality is uncomfortable and correct. A record that is 92% complete is not 92% as useful as a complete record; in automated transactions it is a source of silent error. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - data quality scorecard - remediation queue - blocking event log Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Material Master Governance
text: Material Master Governance policy material master governance · operational policy · version 1.0.0 Defines ownership of material master data, the boundary between procurement and supply chain, and the standard against which material records are complete and unique. --- Purpose The boundary between what is bought and what is received is where physical procurement processes fail. This policy makes ownership explicit — procurement owns the data, supply chain owns the custody — so that neither side can assume the other has closed the loop. Statement Procurement owns the creation, enrichment and quality of material master records. Supply Chain owns physical custody, warehouse receipt and inventory posting. The receipt path for each material shall be declared on the material record and shall be unambiguous as to who confirms quantity and who owns variance. Material records shall be unique, and a creation that matches an existing material within tolerance shall be blocked for steward review. Rules - Material records must be complete against the published required-field standard. - A duplicate search precedes every creation. - The receipt path is mandatory on the material record before any purchase order is raised against it. - Material master changes are impact-analysed against open transactions before being applied. - Procurement shall not post inventory quantities; Supply Chain shall not create material master records. Applies to - - Proc 3.4 - - Proc 4.3 Enforcement Rationale Duplicated materials fragment spend and destroy leverage; ambiguous quantity ownership creates stock that nobody owns. Both are cheap to prevent at creation and expensive to fix later. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - material master change log - duplicate check result - receipt path coverage Related None. title: Procurement Policy of Record
text: Procurement Policy of Record policy procurement policy of record · operational policy · version 1.0.0 The single authoritative statement of how procurement is to be run in this organisation: the obligations that hold across every category, the framework itself as the policy artefact, and the requirement that practice follows the published process. --- Purpose Procurement policy is usually scattered across a policy portal, category playbooks, buyer habits and unwritten rules. This policy establishes one location, and makes the process framework — versioned in Git and published through the management system — the authoritative description of how procurement is performed. Statement All procurement activity shall be performed in accordance with the published process objects in the Procurement Process Framework. Where practice diverges from a published process, the divergence shall be either corrected or the process shall be amended through the co-design process. No process shall be executed by an AI agent that is not published in the framework with an active status and an explicit delegation declaration. Rules - The framework repository is the single source of truth; the management system is its published view, not a second copy. - Every process has a named owner and a review date. An overdue review is automatically flagged and the process is not served to agents at L2 or above. - Local deviations are permitted only as recorded exceptions with an owner and an expiry date. - Practitioner contributions are made as pull requests and reviewed by at least one domain peer and the process owner. Applies to - - Proc 1.1 - - Proc 1.2 - - Proc 1.3 - - Proc 1.4 - - Proc 1.5 - - Proc 1.6 - - Proc 1.7 Enforcement Rationale A process framework that is not the operating standard is documentation. Making the published framework authoritative removes the gap between what is written and what is done, and gives AI agents a single, versioned thing to obey. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - framework release tag - process review dates - exception register Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Segregation of Duties
text: Segregation of Duties policy segregation of duties · compliance policy · version 1.0.0 Prohibits any single person or agent from preparing, approving and executing the same transaction, and defines the compensating controls where separation is not practicable. --- Purpose Most procurement fraud is not sophisticated; it is one person able to do three things in sequence. Segregation of duties is the oldest control in the discipline and the one most often lost as organisations automate. Statement No individual or AI agent shall both prepare a transaction and approve it, and no individual or agent shall approve a transaction they prepared. Where separation is not practicable due to scale or role design, a compensating control shall be documented and reviewed by the Delegation Review Board. Rules - The preparer of a requisition, purchase order, invoice or award may not be its approver. - An AI agent acting as preparer may never act as approver of the same record. - Segregation checks are enforced at routing time and are logged. - Breaches are reported to the Delegation Review Board within one business day. Applies to - - Proc 3.1 - - Proc 3.2 - - Proc 4.1 - - Proc 4.2 - - Proc 5.2 - - Proc 6.1 Enforcement Rationale As agents take on preparation work, the segregation boundary shifts rather than disappears. The rule is written so that the agent occupies the preparer role and a human occupies the approver role — permanently. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - segregation check log - breach register Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Supplier Onboarding and Due Diligence
text: Supplier Onboarding and Due Diligence policy supplier onboarding · supplier policy · version 1.0.0 Requires due diligence, sanctions screening and independent banking verification before a supplier may transact, and prohibits any activation that bypasses it. --- Purpose Onboarding is the gate through which every future transaction with a supplier passes. An incomplete gate means the organisation is transacting with someone it has not verified — and it will keep doing so indefinitely. Statement A supplier shall be granted transactable status only when due diligence is complete, sanctions screening is clear, banking data is independently verified and the supplier master record is complete. No agent shall activate a supplier that has not satisfied every mandatory element, and a screening result shall never be overridden by an agent. Rules - Due diligence is refreshed annually for critical suppliers and on trigger events. - Sanctions screening matches are escalated to the compliance officer and never auto-cleared. - Banking data is verified through an independent channel before first activation. - Expedited onboarding for operational urgency requires sponsor and risk approval, with full due diligence completed within 10 working days. - An inactive or blocked supplier may not transact. Applies to - - Proc 6.1 - - Proc 6.2 - - Proc 3.1 Enforcement Rationale The gate has to be absolute to be worth anything. A single bypass — a well-meaning expedited path — turns the control into theatre, and expedited paths are exactly where bypasses accumulate. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - onboarding record - due diligence pack id - screening result - expedited onboardings Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Supplier Payment Terms
text: Supplier Payment Terms policy supplier payment terms · financial policy · version 1.0.0 Governs the payment terms offered to suppliers, the use of early-payment discounts, and the requirement that term improvements be passed to the supplier and reflected in the systems that calculate due dates. --- Purpose Payment terms are a negotiated commercial position with a real cost. They are frequently agreed in a negotiation, captured in a contract, and then never actually applied because the transactional system still holds the old terms. Statement Payment terms shall be negotiated as part of the commercial schedule and shall be reflected in the transactional systems before the first invoice under the contract is processed. Early-payment discounts shall be captured wherever the cost of liquidity is favourable. Supplier-facing due dates shall be calculated from the contractual terms, not from a default. Rules - Payment terms are recorded in the contract and published to transactional systems via Proc 3.5. - A discount is captured where the liquidity cost is below the discount value. - Due dates presented to suppliers are computed from the published contractual terms. - Term deviations agreed informally are not enforceable and shall be formalised. Applies to - - Proc 3.3 - - Proc 3.5 - - Proc 5.2 - - Proc 5.4 - - Proc 1.6 Enforcement Rationale A discount that is claimed but not captured, or a term agreed but not published, is a value leak that only a reconciliation between contract and system reveals. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - discount capture report - terms reconciliation log Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Supplier Performance Management
text: Supplier Performance Management policy supplier performance · supplier policy · version 1.0.0 Requires that supplier performance be measured against contracted service levels, reviewed with the supplier, and acted upon, and that the results feed renewal and sourcing decisions. --- Purpose Performance data that is collected but not acted upon is a cost with no benefit. This policy requires the loop to close: measure, review, agree action, and feed the result into the commercial decision. Statement Every strategic supplier shall have a defined scorecard measured against contracted service levels, reviewed with the supplier at a defined cadence, and — where performance falls below the agreed threshold — subject to a tracked development or corrective action plan. Performance results shall be an input to every renewal and re-sourcing decision. Rules - Scorecards are defined per contract and use contracted service levels as the measure. - Measurements are supported by evidence and carry a retrieval date. - A scorecard below threshold triggers a tracked action with a named owner and due date. - Where data is missing, the scorecard is marked not measurable; performance is never inferred from incomplete data. - Performance results are visible to the supplier. Applies to - - Proc 6.4 - - Proc 6.2 - - Proc 1.6 - - Proc 1.2 Enforcement Rationale A supplier that performs badly should not first learn it at renewal. Regular review converts performance management from a retrospective judgement into an operating routine. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - scorecard inputs - review minutes - action tracking Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Sustainability and ESG in Procurement
text: Sustainability and ESG in Procurement policy sustainability and esg · esg policy · version 1.0.0 Requires ESG expectations to be translated into supplier requirements, data to be collected with provenance, claims to be verified, and progress to be reported without overstatement. --- Purpose ESG procurement fails quietly — through self-declared data treated as fact, through unverified claims in disclosures, and through requirements so heavy that smaller suppliers are excluded. This policy addresses all three. Statement Supplier ESG data shall be collected with provenance recorded per data point. Self-declared data shall be labelled as self-declared and scored differently from verified data. ESG criteria shall be proportionate to supplier size. Sustainability claims shall not be asserted externally beyond the level of verification obtained. Rules - Every ESG data point records its source and retrieval date. - Verified and self-declared data are scored on separate scales. - Requirements are proportionate; a simplified evidence route is available for smaller suppliers. - Material claims are verified at a defined sampling rate. - External disclosure is limited to what the verification supports. Applies to - - Proc 1.7 - - Proc 3.1 - - Proc 3.3 - - Proc 6.1 Enforcement Rationale The credibility risk to a sustainability programme is greater than the operational risk. One overstated claim damages every data point around it. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - assessment inputs - verification status - disclosure pack id Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Thresholds and Approvals
text: Thresholds and Approvals policy thresholds and approvals · financial policy · version 1.0.0 Defines the approval matrix — who approves what, at what value, and under which delegation — and the aggregation rule that prevents value being split to evade it. --- Purpose Approval matrices fail in two ways: they are ambiguous about who may approve what, or they are evaded by splitting. This policy addresses both, and it is the reference against which every AI delegation threshold in the framework is expressed. Statement No commitment of spend shall be made without approval by the role designated for that value band. Approval requirements shall be computed on an aggregated value across related requisitions within a rolling window, so that a commitment may not be reduced below a threshold by subdivision. Delegated approval limits shall be recorded, time-bound and revocable. Rules - Thresholds are expressed in the currency of record and reviewed annually. - Related requisitions are aggregated by requester, supplier, category and time window before threshold evaluation. - A delegated approver may not approve a request they prepared. - An expedited approval outside the matrix requires a documented reason and retrospective review. Applies to - - Proc 2.1 - - Proc 3.2 - - Proc 4.1 - - Proc 4.2 - - Proc 5.2 - - Proc 5.4 Enforcement Rationale A threshold that can be evaded by subdivision is a suggestion. Aggregation converts a nominal control into a real one, and it is precisely the control that bounds autonomous agent behaviour. Exceptions No exceptions are granted under this policy. Compliance evidence - approval matrix version - aggregation log - expedited approvals Related None. Change log Version Date Author Change --- --- --- --- 1.0.0 2026-01-15 Collabior Co-design Initial policy drafted.

title: Align Global Strategy
path: Procurement > Strategy and Performance > Align Global Strategy
text: Align Global Strategy Proc 1.1 · Procurement Strategy and Performance Align Global Strategy Translates enterprise objectives into a procurement strategy: the value procurement will create, the categories in scope, the spend under management and the levers available to deliver it. --- Purpose Procurement cannot execute a strategy it does not own. This process establishes the enterprise procurement strategy as a first-class business artefact, aligned to enterprise goals, and published so that every downstream process — intake, sourcing, contract — can be evaluated against it. title: Award Recommendation
text: Award Recommendation skills award recommendation · howto · version 1.0.0 How to write an award recommendation that an approver can act on in minutes, and that remains defensible months later. --- When to use this skill After evaluation, when presenting the award for approval. Prerequisites - Completed evaluation scorecard - Consolidated scores Method 1. State the outcome Name the supplier, the price, the term and the total cost of ownership — not the unit price alone. 2. Show the basis Present the score against each locked criterion and the margin over the next bid. 3. Disclose the exceptions List every requirement the winner did not meet perfectly, and why that was acceptable. Hiding this is how a recommendation fails at approval. 4. Give the alternative State what the second choice would have delivered and at what cost, so the approver can judge the trade-off. 5. State the risk Name the risk being carried by this award and who owns it. Outputs - Approved award recommendation Quality bar The recommendation answers: who, at what price, on what basis, against which criteria, with what exceptions, and what the alternative was. Anything it does not answer is missing. Anti-patterns - A recommendation that needs a meeting to explain. - Omitting the runner-up and the margin, which the approver will ask for anyway. - Framing the decision in terms of the relationship rather than the criteria. title: Market Benchmarking
text: Market Benchmarking skills benchmarking · analysis · version 1.0.0 How to establish what a fair price is for a given requirement, using comparable data rather than assertion, and how to cite it so the finding survives challenge. --- When to use this skill Before a negotiation, when validating a savings figure, and when setting an internal target for a category. Prerequisites - A specific, comparable requirement definition - Access to external benchmark data Method 1. Define the comparable State precisely what is being compared — volume, specification, service level, term, geography, delivery model. Benchmarking without this is price-shopping. 2. Collect the comparables Gather multiple independent data points. Record source, date and basis for each. 3. Normalise Adjust for scope, scale, term and conditions so the figures are genuinely comparable. 4. Position State where the current position sits relative to the comparables, and how confident that statement is. 5. Cite Attach the source and date to every figure used downstream, so it can be re-verified rather than re-argued. Outputs - Benchmark analysis with cited sources - Price position statement Quality bar Every benchmark figure cites a source, a date and the comparability basis. An uncited number is not a benchmark. Anti-patterns - Comparing a premium requirement against a commodity benchmark. - Citing a single data point as a market range. - Using a benchmark that is older than the market movement it is used to explain. title: Bid Evaluation
text: Bid Evaluation skills bid evaluation · judgement · version 1.0.0 How to evaluate bids against pre-declared criteria consistently, evidencing every score so the evaluation can be reconstructed later. --- When to use this skill After an RFx closes. Prerequisites - Published, locked evaluation criteria - Approved evaluation panel - Received bids Method 1. Screen for compliance first Establish which bids meet the mandatory requirements. Only compliant bids are evaluated on quality. 2. Evaluate criterion by criterion Complete one criterion across all bids before moving to the next. Comparing across bids within a criterion reduces anchoring. 3. Score with evidence For each score, record the specific part of the bid that justifies it. Not a general impression — a reference. 4. Consolidate and surface divergence Compare evaluator scores and highlight where they diverge most. That divergence points to ambiguity in the requirement. 5. Re-read the criteria After scoring, re-read the locked criteria. If the criteria could not distinguish between bids, the event was designed poorly — say so. Outputs - Completed evaluation scorecard - Consolidated scores with divergence flagged Quality bar Every score carries the evidence that produced it. An evaluator's score without evidence is an opinion and does not survive audit. Anti-patterns - Reading one bid fully and the others quickly. - Comparing bids against each other rather than against the criteria. - Adjusting a score after seeing the consolidated result without recording it. title: Budget Validation
text: Budget Validation skills budget validation · judgement · version 1.0.0 How to verify that a commitment can be funded — checking available balance, encumbrances, period, category and the consequences of committing against a reserved balance. --- When to use this skill Before a requisition is approved or released, and before any autonomous order is issued. Prerequisites - Budget position and encumbrance data - Cost centre and category of the requirement Method 1. Identify the funding source Determine the cost centre, category and budget line the commitment belongs to. 2. Read the available position Take the ledger balance, subtract outstanding encumbrances and reservations. 3. Check the period and category Confirm the budget period is open and the spend is permitted within the category's restrictions. 4. Check the concentration Confirm the commitment does not breach a volume, supplier or category concentration limit. 5. Encumber and record Encumber the amount with a reference to the requisition, so it cannot be spent twice. Outputs - Budget check result - Encumbrance Quality bar The check reflects commitments already made, not only the unspent balance. A balance that ignores encumbrances is not a balance. Anti-patterns - Checking the nominal balance without outstanding encumbrances. - Allowing commitment against a reserved or ring-fenced budget. - Allowing commitment outside the budget period. AI delegation Related - - skills catalogue match

title: Catalogue Matching
text: Catalogue Matching skills catalogue match · judgement · version 1.0.0 How to match a requirement against approved catalogue items and contracted supply, and to explain the match well enough for a requester to disagree with it. --- When to use this skill At intake, and again before a purchase order is issued. Prerequisites - Approved catalogue - Contracted pricing data - The requirement specification Method 1. Extract the requirement attributes Identify the attributes that determine suitability — specification, size, capacity, service level, certification. 2. Retrieve candidates Search the approved catalogue and contracted items for candidates matching those attributes. 3. Score and rank Rank on suitability first, then on price and terms. Never rank on price alone. 4. Check price and terms Confirm the catalogue price is at or below the current contracted price for the same requirement. 5. Explain State the matched item, the matching attributes and the residual gap, so a requester can accept or reject it. Outputs - Catalogue match result with explanation - Reuse or new-source recommendation Quality bar Every recommendation names the item, the matching attributes and the price basis. If the explanation is missing, the match is not usable. Anti-patterns - Matching on the item description alone, ignoring specification attributes. - Accepting a substitute that meets the description but not the requirement. - Forcing a match because something in the catalogue is better than nothing. AI delegation Related - - skills budget validation

title: Category Strategy Development
text: Category Strategy Development skills category strategy development · playbook · version 1.0.0 How to turn portfolio analysis into a category strategy that a practitioner can actually execute: demand profile, sourcing levers, savings plan, risk profile and review calendar. --- When to use this skill When creating or refreshing a category strategy, and when a sourcing event needs to be justified against a strategy. Prerequisites - Portfolio analysis completed - Category spend data within six months Method 1. Characterise demand Describe what is bought, by whom, how often, and what drives the volume. Demand drivers determine which levers are viable. 2. Assess supply structure Map the supplier base, concentration, switching costs and the credible alternatives for each significant requirement. 3. Select and size levers For each candidate lever, state the value mechanism — aggregation, competition, standardisation, negotiation, cost reduction, demand reduction — and size it against the spend. 4. Sequence against capacity Order the levers by value per unit of organisational change consumed. A strategy that ignores change capacity is aspirational. 5. Set the review rhythm Define the triggers that force the strategy to be revisited: market change, performance failure, contract renewal, new regulation. Outputs - Draft category strategy - Sourcing lever backlog - Savings plan and review calendar Quality bar Every lever names its value mechanism, its owner and its expected cycle time. A lever without a value mechanism is a wish. Anti-patterns - Copying the previous year's strategy and changing the dates. - Listing sourcing levers without sizing them. - Setting a savings ambition before the baseline is finance-validated. title: Contract Clause Review
text: Contract Clause Review skills clause review · checklist · version 1.0.0 How to review a contract against the organisation's standard positions, identify the deviations that matter, and escalate the ones that do. --- When to use this skill During internal legal review, and when a supplier returns a marked-up template. Prerequisites - Clause playbook - Deviation register from the template Method 1. Diff against the template Compare the received contract to the approved template and list every deviation. Automate the diff; do not read it. 2. Categorise by risk Liability, indemnity, termination, payment terms, IP, data protection, exclusivity, price escalation, audit rights, service levels. 3. Assess the consequential ones For each material deviation, state the realistic exposure in the context of this deal's value and duration. 4. Recommend Accept, amend with proposed wording, or escalate to the Delegation Review Board with a business justification. 5. Record the precedent Record any accepted deviation so it becomes visible to the next negotiation — accepted deviations are how playbooks erode. Outputs - Reviewed contract - Deviation assessment with recommendation Quality bar Every deviation from the playbook is listed, categorised by risk, and given a recommendation of accept, amend or escalate. None are silently accepted. Anti-patterns - Reading a marked-up contract linearly and reacting to the first surprising clause. - Accepting a liability increase because the deal is urgent. - Ignoring the data protection clauses because this is a low-data engagement. AI delegation Related - - skills template filling

title: Contract Negotiation
text: Contract Negotiation skills contract negotiation · playbook · version 1.0.0 How to prepare for, conduct and close a contract negotiation: the position, the fallback sequence, and the discipline of never conceding without a trade. --- When to use this skill Before any contract discussion with a supplier. Prerequisites - Approved template and clause playbook - Benchmarked price position - Defined walk-away position Method 1. Set the position and the walk-away Define the target, the acceptable range and the point at which you stop. Agree both internally before the conversation. 2. Build the fallback sequence Pre-agree which concession you make first, second and third, and what you get for each. Never improvise the sequence live. 3. Trade, never gift Every concession is exchanged. A longer term for a lower price; a volume commitment for a service level; a payment term for a discount. 4. Watch the late clauses The final exchange is where pressure is applied. Do not accept a late change without re-running the approval for the new position. 5. Capture the value Record the price-down, the term improvement and the obligation gained, and feed them into the contract and the transactional systems. Outputs - Negotiation plan with fallback sequence - Executed amendment with captured value Quality bar Every concession in the final position has a corresponding concession obtained, and is recorded with its value. Anti-patterns - Conceding unilaterally to preserve goodwill that was never tested. - Negotiating without knowing the benchmark. - Accepting a term change in the final minutes to avoid an extension. title: Supplier ESG Assessment
text: Supplier ESG Assessment skills esg assessment · analysis · version 1.0.0 How to assess a supplier's sustainability performance with proportionate rigour, distinguishing what is self-declared from what is verified. --- When to use this skill During onboarding, at annual refresh, and when ESG criteria are applied in a sourcing event. Prerequisites - Published ESG methodology - Materiality threshold agreed Method 1. Establish materiality Define which environmental and social dimensions matter for this category and why. 2. Collect with provenance Record source, date and self-declared or verified status for every data point. 3. Score separately Score verified and self-declared data on separate scales and present both. 4. Set proportionate requirements Scale the evidence requirement to the supplier's size and the category's materiality. 5. Verify a sample Verify the material claims at a defined rate and record the outcome honestly. Outputs - ESG scorecard with provenance - Assessment confidence statement Quality bar Each data point records its source and date. Self-declared and verified data are visibly separated on the scorecard. Anti-patterns - Averaging self-declared and verified data into a single score. - Weighting an unevidenced ESG claim equally to a verified one. - Requiring disproportionate evidence from smaller suppliers. title: Invoice Exception Resolution
text: Invoice Exception Resolution skills exception resolution · playbook · version 1.0.0 How to clear an invoice exception efficiently: classify it, package the context, resolve it, and fix the cause so it does not recur. --- When to use this skill Whenever an invoice is held or fails to match. Prerequisites - A classified exception - Access to the invoice, PO, receipt and contract records Method 1. Classify before acting Assign the reason code first. The code determines the owner, the route and the expected resolution time. 2. Package the context Assemble the invoice, PO, receipt, contract clause, discrepancy and prior attempts into a single package for the owner. 3. Investigate the cause Determine what actually went wrong — a wrong price, a missing receipt, a late delivery, a mis-keyed invoice, a data error. 4. Choose the resolution Correct the record, dispute with the supplier, write off, or cancel. Consider recovery probability and cost of pursuit. 5. Fix the cause Raise the cause into the improvement backlog with the volume it explains. Repeat exceptions are a process defect. Outputs - Resolution decision - Root-cause record Quality bar Each exception is closed with a decision and a cause. The cause is recorded even when the resolution was simple — the repetition data is the point. Anti-patterns - Clearing the exception without recording the cause. - Returning the invoice to the supplier as the default resolution. - Fixing the same recurring cause by handling the symptom again. AI delegation Related - - skills payment release

title: Master Data Quality Management
text: Master Data Quality Management skills master data quality · howto · version 1.0.0 How to keep master records complete, unique, current and attributable — and how to stop a bad record being used in an automated transaction. --- When to use this skill Whenever master data is created, enriched, changed or consumed by an automated process. Prerequisites - Published data quality rules - A named data owner Method 1. Define the rules per object type Completeness, uniqueness, validity, currency and attribution, published and versioned. 2. Enforce at the point of use The blocking check runs where the record is consumed, not only where it was created. 3. Reuse before create Search for an existing fit before creating. Duplicates are cheaper to prevent than to merge. 4. Prioritise remediation by impact Fix the records that affect the most value, not the ones that are easiest to count. 5. Measure and publish Score continuously, publish by owner, and treat a falling score as an operational risk. Outputs - Quality scorecard - Remediation queue - Blocking events Quality bar A record failing a blocking rule is not used in an automated transaction. The rule is enforced by the system, not by a person remembering it. Anti-patterns - Treating completeness as a percentage target rather than a rule. - Letting incomplete records flow because the transaction is urgent. - Restating historical data without recording the taxonomy version. title: Supplier Offboarding
text: Supplier Offboarding skills offboarding · checklist · version 1.0.0 How to end a supplier relationship safely: block first, then resolve exposure, then dispose of data, then attest. --- When to use this skill Whenever a supplier relationship ends, for any reason. Prerequisites - A confirmed offboarding trigger - The open commitments and data inventories Method 1. Block transactable status immediately The first step, and irreversible in the session. Exposure takes days to close; the ability to transact must stop now. 2. Inventory open commitments List every open order, invoice, claim, credit and forecast, and disposition each one individually. 3. Revoke access and settle data Remove portal and system access, and have the DPO determine the disposition of every record — including those under hold. 4. Notify and close Communicate the outcome, the final settlement position and what the supplier must do. 5. Attest Record who did what, and confirm no post-termination transactions occurred. Outputs - Blocked status - Resolved commitments - Data disposition record - Offboarding attestation Quality bar No supplier can transact after termination, every open commitment has a disposition, and every record has a retention decision. Anti-patterns - Resolving payments and data first, and blocking last. - Archiving the supplier record while leaving it transactable. - Purging data that is under legal or contractual hold. title: Payment Release
text: Payment Release skills payment release · checklist · version 1.0.0 How to release a payment safely: scheduling, discount capture, independent bank verification, dual control and reconciliation. --- When to use this skill Before every payment run. Prerequisites - Approved invoices - Verified supplier banking data - Dual control in place Method 1. Schedule the run Group approved invoices, apply discount deadlines and contractual terms, and confirm the cash position. 2. Verify banking data Confirm the destination account is the verified account, through a channel independent of any recent change request. 3. Check holds and flags Exclude every invoice under a hold, a fraud flag or an unresolved exception. 4. Obtain dual authorisation Two named people authorise the run. An agent may prepare and summarise the run; it may never authorise it. 5. Release, remit and reconcile Release the file, send remittance advice, and reconcile the confirmation back to the ledger the same day. Outputs - Payment run - Bank verification record - Reconciliation record Quality bar Every payment can be traced to an approved invoice, a verified bank account and a named release authorisation. Any of the three missing means it does not run. Anti-patterns - Releasing payments for suppliers whose bank data changed recently without independent verification. - Running payments for invoices still on hold. - Assuming a failed payment file simply needs resubmitting.
