title: Purchase Order Creation
text: Purchase Order Creation skills po creation · howto · version 1.0.0 How to build a purchase order that is complete on issue — every field a supplier needs to act, and every field a matcher needs to reconcile. --- When to use this skill When creating or amending a purchase order. Prerequisites - Approved requisition - Contract pricing - Complete supplier and material master data Method 1. Build from the approved requisition Line items, quantities and the cost centre come from the requisition. Do not re-derive them. 2. Apply contract pricing Pull the price, currency, unit of measure, payment terms and validity from the contract. Record the price source. 3. Complete the commercial fields Delivery address, contact, delivery date, tax treatment, freight terms and any service start date. 4. Validate Run completeness and policy validation. Blocking validation failures stop the order; warnings are reviewed. 5. Issue and confirm Issue the order, transmit it to the supplier, and monitor for acknowledgement. Outputs - Issued purchase order - PO validation results Quality bar The supplier can act on the order without a phone call, and the accounts payable matcher can reconcile it against a receipt without a query. Anti-patterns - Free-text descriptions instead of item references. - Leaving delivery dates blank and relying on a separate email. - Omitting unit of measure or currency on a multi-currency order. AI delegation Related - - skills template filling

title: Procurement Portfolio Analysis
text: Procurement Portfolio Analysis skills portfolio analysis · analysis · version 1.0.0 How to read the spend cube and turn it into a procurement portfolio view: concentration, tail spend, maverick spend, category volatility and the structural signals that drive strategy. --- When to use this skill At the start of strategy work, whenever a category boundary is questioned, and whenever the organisation needs to know where its leverage actually is. Prerequisites - A 12-month spend cube - An agreed category taxonomy Method 1. Establish the baseline Reconcile the spend cube to the finance ledger for the period. Discrepancies above 0.5% are resolved before analysis begins. 2. Map concentration Compute the share of spend with the top one, five and ten suppliers per category, and the share held by suppliers with no contract. 3. Segment the tail Quantify transactions below the sourcing threshold. High tail share means the process, not the suppliers, is the problem. 4. Detect maverick spend Identify spend with suppliers outside the approved panel, and spend above contract price for contracted suppliers. 5. Read volatility Examine month-to-month and year-on-year variation. Volatile categories need different sourcing levers than stable ones — aggregation versus direct negotiation. Outputs - Concentration analysis by category and supplier - Tail and maverick spend quantification - Volatility and trend indicators Quality bar Every figure is traceable to the spend cube and reproducible. Totals reconcile to finance. A number that cannot be reproduced is not in the analysis. Anti-patterns - Analysing supplier names rather than categories, because the taxonomy is uncomfortable. - Mixing periods or currencies without restating, producing a trend that is an artefact. - Reporting category share without the absolute value behind it. AI delegation Related - - skills category strategy development

title: Process Improvement Design
text: Process Improvement Design skills process improvement · howto · version 1.0.0 How to turn operational evidence into a framework change: identify the friction, size the benefit, design the change across every artefact it touches, and validate before publishing. --- When to use this skill When cycle times miss target, when exception rates are high, or when a framework release is being prepared. Prerequisites - Process telemetry available - Named process owner engaged Method 1. Find the friction Locate the step where time is actually spent, not where people believe it is spent. Compare telemetry against the exception narrative. 2. Size it Quantify the cost of the current state — cycle time, effort, exceptions, leakage — so the benefit can be compared against the effort. 3. Design the whole change Specify the change to the process object, the skill, the policy and the template. A half-change produces the wrong behaviour. 4. Validate Pilot with a real volume of work, with the practitioner who will do it. Watch the step, do not ask about it. 5. Publish Release through the co-design governance, then measure against the baseline you captured. Outputs - Improvement proposal - Change set across process, skill, policy and template - Pilot evidence Quality bar The proposal names every artefact it touches. A change to a process step alone is rejected as incomplete. Anti-patterns - Improving the documentation of a process without changing the process. - Declaring a benefit without a measurement point and a baseline. - Changing a process without changing the template that implements it. AI delegation Related - - skills portfolio analysis

title: Requirement Analysis
text: Requirement Analysis skills requirement analysis · playbook · version 1.0.0 How to convert a business need into a specification precise enough to source, evaluate and contract against without further clarification. --- When to use this skill Before drafting an RFx, when a request is returned for correction, and when evaluation criteria are defined. Prerequisites - A qualified, budgeted requirement - The relevant category strategy Method 1. Separate need from solution State the business outcome the requirement serves before describing any product or service. 2. Make it testable Express each requirement so that a bid can be scored against it and a delivered item can be checked against it. 3. Cover the whole lifecycle Include implementation, service levels, support, training, end-of-life and data obligations. These are where the cost is usually hidden. 4. Define the criteria now Draft the evaluation criteria and weighting at the same time as the specification, before any supplier is approached. 5. Sanity-check for ambiguity Have someone outside the project read it. Ask them to tell you what would win. That is your criteria. Outputs - Requirements specification - Draft evaluation criteria Quality bar Two independent evaluators, given only the specification, would reach the same conclusion about which bid is better. Anti-patterns - Writing the requirement around a preferred supplier's product. - Leaving evaluation criteria implicit so they can be adjusted later. - Ignoring the service and support requirements because the price is the headline. AI delegation Related - - skills bid evaluation

title: RFx Authoring
text: RFx Authoring skills rfx authoring · howto · version 1.0.0 How to assemble a complete, unbiased and evaluable request for proposal from an approved template, so that suppliers respond comparably and the award can be defended. --- When to use this skill When creating an RFx package for publication. Prerequisites - Approved sourcing strategy - Approved requirements specification - Approved RFx template Method 1. Start from the approved template Never draft an RFx from scratch. The template encodes the organisation's legal and commercial standard position. 2. Fill only what is fillable Populate the declared fillable fields. Leave locked sections — legal text, commercial positions — as the template defines them. 3. Make responses comparable Require the same structure and the same response basis from every bidder. Incomparable responses make evaluation a matter of opinion. 4. State the evaluation up front Publish the criteria and weighting so bidders can aim their response, and so the process is auditable afterwards. 5. Sanity-check for bias Read the package as a supplier who would benefit from a particular wording. Remove what only that supplier would satisfy. Outputs - Published RFx event - Locked evaluation criteria Quality bar The package answers every question a supplier would reasonably ask, and reveals no information that would favour one bidder. title: Third-Party Risk Assessment
text: Third-Party Risk Assessment skills risk assessment · judgement · version 1.0.0 How to identify, score and mitigate third-party risk consistently across categories, using a published methodology rather than intuition. --- When to use this skill At supplier onboarding, on material spend changes, on incident, and at each quarterly risk review. Prerequisites - Published risk methodology - Risk appetite stated by the organisation Method 1. Identify Enumerate risks across financial, operational, concentration, continuity, compliance, data and ESG dimensions. 2. Score Apply the published likelihood and impact matrix. Show the working for every score so it can be challenged. 3. Mitigate For each risk above the appetite threshold, name the action, the owner, the cost and the date. An action without a cost is not funded. 4. Decide For residual risk above appetite, escalate to the Delegation Review Board for acceptance, mitigation or supplier exit. Outputs - Scored risk assessment - Mitigation plan with owners - Escalation pack for high-rated risks Quality bar Every score cites the evidence that produced it. A risk rated without evidence is an opinion, and the register cannot hold opinions. Anti-patterns - Rating risk from the supplier's reputation rather than their data. - Scoring every risk in a band rather than differentiating. - Recording a risk with no owner because nobody wants to hold it. title: Savings Validation
text: Savings Validation skills savings validation · judgement · version 1.0.0 How to define, evidence and validate a savings figure so that it survives contact with finance and can be defended a year later. --- When to use this skill Whenever a savings figure is claimed, reported or committed to a plan. Prerequisites - Finance-validated baseline - Contract and award records Method 1. Fix the baseline Establish the finance-validated baseline. Where no validated baseline exists, report the category as not measurable rather than estimating. 2. Classify the value mechanism Price reduction, volume reduction, demand reduction, cost avoidance, working capital. Each is measured differently and cannot be added without care. 3. Evidence the stage Identified requires a benchmark. Validated requires finance agreement. Negotiated requires a signed award. Realised requires post-award spend. 4. Measure realised Compare post-award spend against the baseline over the defined window, allowing for volume and mix change. 5. Investigate leakage Identify value lost between stages and its cause. Leakage is usually a process defect, not a negotiation failure. Outputs - Stage-evidenced savings entry - Validated savings figure - Leakage analysis Quality bar Every savings figure carries its baseline, its method, its evidence and its measurement window. An unevidenced figure is not reported. Anti-patterns - Using a spend-based baseline where a price-based one is correct. - Claiming savings at award rather than at realisation. - Counting the same saving in a category strategy and a savings funnel. title: Supplier Market Analysis
text: Supplier Market Analysis skills supplier market analysis · analysis · version 1.0.0 How to understand the supply market for a requirement — who can supply it, how concentrated it is, and how credible each alternative is. --- When to use this skill Before building a shortlist, before recommending single source, and when a category strategy names a market risk. Prerequisites - A defined requirement - Access to market intelligence Method 1. Define the supply boundary Establish what is and is not part of the addressable supply for this requirement. 2. Map the current structure Identify suppliers, their share, their capacity and the switching costs that keep them in place. 3. Widen the universe Include suppliers from adjacent segments, other geographies and new entrants. Record why each is credible. 4. Assess credibility Test each candidate against capability, capacity, financial standing, risk and ESG. Remove those that fail. 5. Judge market depth Ask whether three suppliers could credibly serve the whole volume. If not, the event is a negotiation and should be run as one. Outputs - Market structure assessment - Candidate supplier universe with rationale Quality bar Every candidate in the universe has a stated reason for inclusion and evidence of capability. A long list with no reasoning is not analysis. Anti-patterns - Building the universe from existing suppliers only. - Including a supplier that has not passed due diligence. - Judging market depth from the number of names rather than their capacity to serve the volume. title: Supplier Onboarding

Validate the entity before anything else. 2. Check for an existing record Search by legal entity, tax identifier and bank account. A duplicate here becomes a duplicate payment later. 3. Run due diligence and screening Financial standing, compliance, sanctions, ESG. Escalate any screening match — never auto-clear it. 4. Verify banking independently Call back on a number held independently of the request to confirm the account. 5. Create, approve and activate Create the master record, approve the risk tier, then activate to transactable. Order matters: nothing transactable until all of it is done. Outputs - Supplier master record - Due diligence pack - Transactable activation Quality bar No supplier is transactable until every mandatory element is complete. title: Supplier Performance Review
text: Supplier Performance Review skills supplier performance review · playbook · version 1.0.0 How to measure, review and act on supplier performance so that the conversation is evidence-based and ends in an agreed action. --- When to use this skill At each review cycle, after a service level breach, and before a renewal. Prerequisites - A defined scorecard - Contracted service levels - Measurement data with retrieval dates Method 1. Measure against contracted service levels Use the measure that was agreed in the contract, not the one that is easiest to collect. 2. Show the trend Present the trajectory alongside the point score. A supplier improving from 70% is a different conversation from one falling from 95%. 3. Validate with the supplier Share the data and the method. Disagreements about measurement are resolved before the performance conversation, not during it. 4. Agree the action For gaps, agree a specific action with an owner, a date and a measure of success. 5. Feed it forward Carry the result into the renewal decision, the sourcing strategy and the supplier risk tier. Outputs - Supplier scorecard - Performance review record - Development or corrective action plan Quality bar Every score is evidenced and dated, the trend is visible, and the review ends with a specific, owned action. title: Three-Way Matching
text: Three-Way Matching skills three way match · judgement · version 1.0.0 How to match an invoice against the purchase order and the receipt, evaluate the variance against defined tolerances, and explain precisely what does not agree. --- When to use this skill When matching an invoice, and when configuring the matching rules. Prerequisites - Purchase order - Goods receipt or service acceptance - Published tolerance rules Method 1. Match the lines Match invoice lines to PO lines on item, then on quantity, then on price. Record the match method used. 2. Bring in the receipt Compare invoiced quantity against received quantity. An over-invoice against an under-receipt is the classic exception. 3. Evaluate each variance Test price, quantity, unit of measure, tax and payment terms against the published tolerance rules. 4. Explain the exception Name the breach, the magnitude and the likely cause. Route to the owner who can actually resolve it. 5. Protect the tolerance If the same tolerance is breached repeatedly, it is a tolerance problem, not an operator problem — raise it as a process improvement. Outputs - Match result - Variance explanation Quality bar A failed match names the specific breach — which quantity, which price, which term — and the size of it. "Match failed" is not an acceptable output. Anti-patterns - Treating a missing receipt as a zero receipt and matching the invoice. - Comparing invoice price against the catalogue rather than the PO. - Widening tolerance to clear a queue.
